# Cookbook: using `delphi` on repositories that already exist

**This file is generated by running it.** `cookbook.mjs` ran every command below in a checkout of a
public repository that is not ours, and pasted what came back. There are three, chosen to differ:

| | repository | at commit | what it tests | commands | records | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [fractastical/morpholib](https://github.com/fractastical/morpholib) | `befd35cd` (2026-11-22) | Lean proofs that publish no axiom audit | 26 | 15 | 3 inside, 0 outside, 1 cannot-assess; 1 built, 1 refused |
| 2 | [ai/nanoid](https://github.com/ai/nanoid) | `055d1700` (2026-11-05) | README claims checked by scripts, no Lean | 19 | 13 | 2 inside, 0 outside, 1 cannot-assess; 1 built, 1 refused |
| 3 | [fahad-96/wolstenholme-zolotarev](https://github.com/fahad-96/wolstenholme-zolotarev) | `bec02d30` (2026-10-16) | Lean proofs checked as published, in the project's own Lake environment | 15 | 10 | 1 inside, 0 outside, 1 cannot-assess; 1 built, 1 refused |

One installed package ran all three, with no change between them. The commands were not run from our source tree: each
run packed the npm package, installed it into an empty folder and used that copy
(`delphisci-delphi-0.3.0.tgz`, sha256 `312fff9631a92bb8`). The store each run produced is kept beside this
file, and `node tracks/kernel/embed/cookbook.mjs --check` recomputes all three and confirms every record
id printed here is in one of them.

Nothing was pushed to any of these repositories. A run writes only `.delphi/` and `delphi-audit/` in
a scratch checkout.

## Install

```bash
npm install --save-dev https://delphi-mission-control.ashenoy000.workers.dev/blueprint3d/studio-live/tracks/kernel/files/delphisci-delphi-0.3.0.tgz
npx delphi init
```

It needs Node 20 or later and has no dependencies. It is not on the npm registry: the address above is
the same tarball these runs used. In the commands below, `delphi` is that installed command.

To check a Lean file, `delphi` runs Lean inside the nearest Lake project above the file, so it sees
your toolchain and your libraries. No Lean on the machine means a Lean law is refused as unchecked. It
is never passed. Laws checked by a script need no Lean at all (example 2).


---

## Example 1. A claim that was true and could not be checked

**The question:** three Lean files in this repository each say they contain no `sorry`. Is that
true, and could a stranger have checked it from the files?

**What the run found:** yes, and no. All 115 theorems and lemmas are accepted by the Lean kernel on its
three standard axioms. None of the three files could show that as published, because none asks Lean to
print the axioms its theorems depend on. One line per theorem fixes it.

Nothing of that repository is redistributed here beyond the one line in each file that states the claim.

### 1. Adopt it

One command, run at the top of the existing repository. It adds a `.delphi/` folder and changes nothing else.

```console
$ delphi init --name morpholib
initialised  .delphi
project      morpholib
store        .delphi/store/nodes.jsonl  (append-only, one record per line, commit it)
method       .delphi/BEST_PRACTICES.md  (generated; regenerate with `delphi best-practices`)
graph        .delphi/graph/index.html   (rewritten after every mint, private to this project)
laws         .delphi/laws/              (put your Lean files here)

Next: record the source of one number you already rely on.
  delphi evidence --kind doi --ref <doi> --quote "<the words it prints>" --where "<table or section>"

Lean files are checked in your own Lake project, found from the file, so they see your
toolchain and your libraries. With no Lean on this machine, `delphi law --lean` is refused
as unchecked, never passed. A law given with --script says on its record that a script
checked it.
```

### 2. Record what the project claims, in its own words

Evidence is a source and the exact words read in it. Here the source is a file in the repository
itself, and the words are the line where it states its claim. A fact is the number in that sentence,
filed under that evidence, with the conditions that pin it down: which file, at which commit.

```console
$ delphi evidence --kind file --ref morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean --quote 'in pure core Lean 4 (zero external dependencies, zero `sorry`s, sub-second kernel check).' --where "line 8, the file's header comment" --retrieved 2026-11-22
evidence k8385c2c983dc1c4c  file:morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean
```

```console
$ delphi fact --statement 'MathOfBiology.lean states that it contains no sorry' --quantity sorry_claimed --value 0 --unit count --condition file=morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean --condition commit=befd35cd --evidence k8385c2c983dc1c4c
fact     kdcbf9d1df9057817  sorry_claimed = 0 count
```

The other two files are recorded the same way:

```console
$ delphi evidence --kind file --ref morphoeval/lean/Ruliobiology.lean --quote 'Kernel-check (0 sorry, 0 custom axioms, no Mathlib):' --where "line 10, the file's header comment" --retrieved 2026-11-22
evidence k8d1011f43d5f7fc6  file:morphoeval/lean/Ruliobiology.lean
```

```console
$ delphi fact --statement 'Ruliobiology.lean states that it contains no sorry' --quantity sorry_claimed --value 0 --unit count --condition file=morphoeval/lean/Ruliobiology.lean --condition commit=befd35cd --evidence k8d1011f43d5f7fc6
fact     k628b6f9ff55fd9b6  sorry_claimed = 0 count
```

```console
$ delphi evidence --kind file --ref morphoeval/lean/LinearResource.lean --quote '(0 sorry, no additional axioms). STATUS: PROTOTYPE — not yet emitted into the KG.' --where "line 7, the file's header comment" --retrieved 2026-11-22
evidence k7b5041a927d1e37c  file:morphoeval/lean/LinearResource.lean
```

```console
$ delphi fact --statement 'LinearResource.lean states that it contains no sorry' --quantity sorry_claimed --value 0 --unit count --condition file=morphoeval/lean/LinearResource.lean --condition commit=befd35cd --evidence k7b5041a927d1e37c
fact     k10511a275f5fa506  sorry_claimed = 0 count
```

**Notice:** try leaving out `--quote`, or `--condition`. The command refuses and says which rule it
broke. That refusal is the method working, not the tool being awkward.

### 3. Ask the kernel to accept the claim as published

```console
$ delphi law --name MathOfBiology_as_published --informal 'Every theorem in this file is accepted by the Lean kernel with no sorry and no added axiom.' --lean morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean
REFUSED  law MathOfBiology_as_published
         - morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean has 76 theorem(s) and no "#print axioms" line: nothing in it can be audited
```

The same for the other two:

```console
$ delphi law --name Ruliobiology_as_published --informal 'Every theorem in this file is accepted by the Lean kernel with no sorry and no added axiom.' --lean morphoeval/lean/Ruliobiology.lean
REFUSED  law Ruliobiology_as_published
         - morphoeval/lean/Ruliobiology.lean has 31 theorem(s) and no "#print axioms" line: nothing in it can be audited
```

```console
$ delphi law --name LinearResource_as_published --informal 'Every theorem in this file is accepted by the Lean kernel with no sorry and no added axiom.' --lean morphoeval/lean/LinearResource.lean
REFUSED  law LinearResource_as_published
         - morphoeval/lean/LinearResource.lean has 8 theorem(s) and no "#print axioms" line: nothing in it can be audited
```

**Notice:** this is not a failed proof. The kernel refused before starting Lean, because a file with
no `#print axioms` line gives nothing to audit: a hand-written `axiom` would pass every search for
`sorry`. "Zero sorry" was true here and unverifiable, which is the common case.

### 4. Make it checkable without touching it

`delphi audit` copies the file into `.delphi/laws/` and appends one audit line per theorem. The
original is only read. Then `delphi law` runs Lean on the copy and records what it printed.

This sparse checkout has no built Mathlib of its own, so for this run `DELPHI_LEAN_PROJECT` named a
Lake project that has one. Each law record says so ("the Lake project named for this check").

```console
$ delphi audit morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean
audit    morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean  sha256 2907c36ca2c36fcd
         76 theorem(s) and lemma(s), 0 axiom-audit line(s) as published, 0 sorry in code, 0 hand-written axiom(s), 0 import(s)
         copy with 76 audit line(s) appended -> .delphi/laws/MathOfBiology.Audited.lean  (the original was only read)
```

```console
$ delphi law --name MathOfBiology_audited --informal 'Every theorem and lemma in this file is accepted by the Lean kernel on its three standard axioms, with no sorry and no hand-written axiom.' --lean MathOfBiology.Audited.lean
law      k2d8d7e578a17676d  MathOfBiology_audited
         .delphi/laws/MathOfBiology.Audited.lean  CHECKED  axioms [Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext]  76 declaration(s) audited
         checked in the Lake project named for this check, leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0
```

```console
$ delphi audit morphoeval/lean/Ruliobiology.lean
audit    morphoeval/lean/Ruliobiology.lean  sha256 79d470f8eb339b95
         31 theorem(s) and lemma(s), 0 axiom-audit line(s) as published, 0 sorry in code, 0 hand-written axiom(s), 0 import(s)
         copy with 31 audit line(s) appended -> .delphi/laws/Ruliobiology.Audited.lean  (the original was only read)
```

```console
$ delphi law --name Ruliobiology_audited --informal 'Every theorem and lemma in this file is accepted by the Lean kernel on its three standard axioms, with no sorry and no hand-written axiom.' --lean Ruliobiology.Audited.lean
law      k9132887d6adcec44  Ruliobiology_audited
         .delphi/laws/Ruliobiology.Audited.lean  CHECKED  axioms [Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext]  31 declaration(s) audited
         checked in the Lake project named for this check, leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0
```

```console
$ delphi audit morphoeval/lean/LinearResource.lean
audit    morphoeval/lean/LinearResource.lean  sha256 94741a6acae4c1cc
         8 theorem(s) and lemma(s), 0 axiom-audit line(s) as published, 0 sorry in code, 0 hand-written axiom(s), 0 import(s)
         copy with 8 audit line(s) appended -> .delphi/laws/LinearResource.Audited.lean  (the original was only read)
```

```console
$ delphi law --name LinearResource_audited --informal 'Every theorem and lemma in this file is accepted by the Lean kernel on its three standard axioms, with no sorry and no hand-written axiom.' --lean LinearResource.Audited.lean
law      kcaa376871942f6a4  LinearResource_audited
         .delphi/laws/LinearResource.Audited.lean  CHECKED  axioms [Quot.sound, propext]  8 declaration(s) audited
         checked in the Lake project named for this check, leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0
```

**Notice:** each law record carries the hash of the exact bytes Lean checked. Edit the file afterwards
and `delphi doctor` will say the record no longer matches.

### 5. Apply the law to the claim

A verdict is a law applied to facts. The check here is a short script kept in the project, so
anyone can read what "inside" meant:

```js
// Is the file's own claim true of the file? Inside when the code holds exactly as many `sorry` as it
// claims and no hand-written axiom. The Lean kernel's acceptance is the law this is applied under;
// this script only counts, so that the verdict names numbers a reader can recount.
import fs from 'node:fs';

export default (values, facts) => {
  const file = facts[0].conditions.file;
  const src = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
  const code = src.replace(/\/-[\s\S]*?-\//g, ' ').replace(/--[^\n]*/g, ' ');
  const sorry = (code.match(/\bsorry\b/g) ?? []).length;
  const axioms = (code.match(/^\s*axiom\s+/gm) ?? []).length;
  return {
    result: sorry === values.sorry_claimed && axioms === 0 ? 'inside' : 'outside',
    detail: `${file}: ${sorry} sorry in code against ${values.sorry_claimed} claimed, ${axioms} hand-written axiom(s)`,
  };
};
```

```console
$ delphi verdict --law k2d8d7e578a17676d --fact kdcbf9d1df9057817 --requires sorry_claimed --check .delphi/checks/claim-matches-file.mjs --label 'MathOfBiology: the zero-sorry claim'
verdict  k1e4d15121973226f  INSIDE  MathOfBiology_audited [MathOfBiology: the zero-sorry claim]
         morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean: 0 sorry in code against 0 claimed, 0 hand-written axiom(s)
```

```console
$ delphi verdict --law k9132887d6adcec44 --fact k628b6f9ff55fd9b6 --requires sorry_claimed --check .delphi/checks/claim-matches-file.mjs --label 'Ruliobiology: the zero-sorry claim'
verdict  kb51caeb94192b4c6  INSIDE  Ruliobiology_audited [Ruliobiology: the zero-sorry claim]
         morphoeval/lean/Ruliobiology.lean: 0 sorry in code against 0 claimed, 0 hand-written axiom(s)
```

```console
$ delphi verdict --law kcaa376871942f6a4 --fact k10511a275f5fa506 --requires sorry_claimed --check .delphi/checks/claim-matches-file.mjs --label 'LinearResource: the zero-sorry claim'
verdict  kc889878ccaef6613  INSIDE  LinearResource_audited [LinearResource: the zero-sorry claim]
         morphoeval/lean/LinearResource.lean: 0 sorry in code against 0 claimed, 0 hand-written axiom(s)
```

The first file's header also says its kernel check is sub-second. Nobody has recorded a timing, so
the honest answer is neither yes nor no:

```console
$ delphi verdict --law k2d8d7e578a17676d --fact kdcbf9d1df9057817 --requires kernel_check_seconds --expr 'kernel_check_seconds < 1' --label 'MathOfBiology: the sub-second claim'
verdict  kcc2a658ba4df8e79  CANNOT-ASSESS  MathOfBiology_audited [MathOfBiology: the sub-second claim]
         missing input(s): kernel_check_seconds
         cannot-assess is not a pass. A build resting on this will be refused.
```

**Notice:** `cannot-assess` is a result, never a pass. In most codebases a check with a missing input
returns true.

### 6. Build something, or be told exactly why not

An artifact resting on the unassessed claim is refused, and the refusal is itself recorded:

```console
$ delphi build --artifact 'a "checks in under a second" badge' --verdict kcc2a658ba4df8e79
REFUSED  a "checks in under a second" badge
         - MathOfBiology_audited (MathOfBiology: the sub-second claim): could not be assessed — missing input(s): kernel_check_seconds

The refusal is itself a record: ka76c8b9868c534e6. It is the shortest list of what would have to
be true for this artifact to be honest, so it is worth publishing rather than hiding.
```

An artifact resting on the three verdicts that held is minted, and its file is hashed into the record:

```console
$ delphi build --artifact 'axiom audit report' --verdict k1e4d15121973226f --verdict kb51caeb94192b4c6 --verdict kc889878ccaef6613 --file delphi-audit/REPORT.md
build    ke73d3f7d102807f4  axiom audit report
         26eab6750063af51       988  delphi-audit/REPORT.md
```

### 7. Read it back

Anything in the store can be walked back to the words it rests on:

```console
$ delphi why badge
refusal  ka76c8b9868c534e6  a "checks in under a second" badge
         - MathOfBiology_audited (MathOfBiology: the sub-second claim): could not be assessed — missing input(s): kernel_check_seconds
  verdict  kcc2a658ba4df8e79  CANNOT-ASSESS  MathOfBiology_audited [MathOfBiology: the sub-second claim]  missing input(s): kernel_check_seconds
    fact     kdcbf9d1df9057817  sorry_claimed = 0 count  [file=morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean, commit=befd35cd]
      evidence k8385c2c983dc1c4c  file:morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean  "in pure core Lean 4 (zero external dependencies, zero `sorry`s, sub-second kern…"  (line 8, the file's header comment)
    law      k2d8d7e578a17676d  MathOfBiology_audited  .delphi/laws/MathOfBiology.Audited.lean -> CHECKED axioms[Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext]
```

```console
$ delphi summary
store    .delphi/store/nodes.jsonl
nodes    15  (3 evidence, 3 fact, 3 law, 4 verdict, 1 refusal, 1 build)
verdicts 3 inside, 0 outside, 1 cannot-assess
builds   1 minted, 1 refused
chain    every id and link recomputed clean
```

### 8. The two commands for CI

```console
$ delphi verify
verified 15 node(s): every id matches its content and every chain link holds
```

```console
$ delphi doctor
note     1 refusal(s) on record. These are the most useful thing in the store to publish: `delphi why <name>` prints what each one was missing.
doctor: 15 node(s) sound — store chain, 3 proof file(s), 1 artifact file(s) all match their recorded hashes; 1 note(s)
```

The axioms listed for each file are the union of what its audited theorems printed.

## Example 2. Numbers in a README, with no proof assistant

**The question:** the README says the library is 117 bytes and has no dependencies. Does the
repository agree with its own README?

**What the run found:** on both counts that can be checked from the files, yes. The manifest lists no
runtime dependency, and the 117 bytes in the README is exactly the limit the project's own size check
enforces. Whether the code *measures* 117 bytes is not something this run can say: it did not install
or run the project's build tools, so that verdict is `cannot-assess` and the badge resting on it was refused.

There is no Lean here. Every law is checked by a script, and every record says so.

### 1. Adopt it

```console
$ delphi init --name nanoid
initialised  .delphi
project      nanoid
store        .delphi/store/nodes.jsonl  (append-only, one record per line, commit it)
method       .delphi/BEST_PRACTICES.md  (generated; regenerate with `delphi best-practices`)
graph        .delphi/graph/index.html   (rewritten after every mint, private to this project)
laws         .delphi/laws/              (put your Lean files here)

Next: record the source of one number you already rely on.
  delphi evidence --kind doi --ref <doi> --quote "<the words it prints>" --where "<table or section>"

Lean files are checked in your own Lake project, found from the file, so they see your
toolchain and your libraries. With no Lean on this machine, `delphi law --lean` is refused
as unchecked, never passed. A law given with --script says on its record that a script
checked it.
```

### 2. Record the claim and what it will be checked against

One line of the README carries both claims, so one piece of evidence carries two facts:

```console
$ delphi evidence --kind file --ref README.md --quote '- **Small.** 117 bytes (minified and brotlied). No dependencies.' --where 'line 13, the feature list' --retrieved 2026-11-05
evidence kab4f4b54ba97a05f  file:README.md
```

```console
$ delphi fact --statement 'The README says the package has no dependencies' --quantity dependencies_claimed --value 0 --unit count --condition file=README.md --condition commit=055d1700 --evidence kab4f4b54ba97a05f
fact     k22a5f0963672709f  dependencies_claimed = 0 count
```

```console
$ delphi fact --statement 'The README gives the size of the nanoid import, minified and brotlied' --quantity size_claimed_bytes --value 117 --unit bytes --condition file=README.md --condition commit=055d1700 --evidence kab4f4b54ba97a05f
fact     k510910c2df0ced51  size_claimed_bytes = 117 bytes
```

The other side of the comparison is a number too, with its own source:

```console
$ delphi evidence --kind file --ref package.json --quote '"limit": "117 B"' --where 'line 77, the first size-limit entry (import { nanoid })' --retrieved 2026-11-05
evidence k0a4fef80fd02ac6b  file:package.json
```

```console
$ delphi fact --statement "The limit the project's own size check enforces on the nanoid import" --quantity size_limit_bytes --value 117 --unit bytes --condition file=package.json --condition commit=055d1700 --evidence k0a4fef80fd02ac6b
fact     k9fe87ec86c266aa2  size_limit_bytes = 117 bytes
```

### 3. State the law, and say what checks it

A statement with nothing behind it is refused:

```console
$ delphi law --name no_runtime_dependencies --informal 'A package has no runtime dependencies when its manifest lists none.'
REFUSED  law no_runtime_dependencies
         - no Lean file and no script: nothing to check
```

Given a script, it is accepted, and the record says a script checked it:

```console
$ delphi law --name no_runtime_dependencies --informal 'A package has no runtime dependencies when its manifest lists none under dependencies, peerDependencies or optionalDependencies.' --script .delphi/checks/manifest-dependencies.mjs
law      k11c8206a7f379eb4  no_runtime_dependencies
         checked by a script, NOT by a proof assistant: .delphi/checks/manifest-dependencies.mjs
```

```console
$ delphi law --name readme_matches_enforced_limit --informal 'A size printed in a README is the size the project holds itself to when it equals the limit its own size check is configured with.' --script 'the expression recorded in each verdict'
law      k360d4af5c47deeec  readme_matches_enforced_limit
         checked by a script, NOT by a proof assistant: the expression recorded in each verdict
```

```console
$ delphi law --name size_within_claim --informal 'A published size holds when the size measured the way the claim says is no larger than the claim.' --script 'the expression recorded in each verdict'
law      k29300f625781417b  size_within_claim
         checked by a script, NOT by a proof assistant: the expression recorded in each verdict
```

The script for the first one, in full:

```js
// Does the manifest list as many runtime dependencies as the README claims? Inside when the counts
// are equal. devDependencies are not counted: they are not installed for a user of the package.
import fs from 'node:fs';

export default (values) => {
  const pkg = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('package.json', 'utf8'));
  const kinds = ['dependencies', 'peerDependencies', 'optionalDependencies'];
  const counts = kinds.map((k) => Object.keys(pkg[k] ?? {}).length);
  const total = counts.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
  return {
    result: total === values.dependencies_claimed ? 'inside' : 'outside',
    detail: `package.json: ${kinds.map((k, i) => `${counts[i]} ${k}`).join(', ')} against ${values.dependencies_claimed} claimed`,
  };
};
```

### 4. Apply each law

```console
verdict  k7c73447fb152f50b  INSIDE  readme_matches_enforced_limit [README size against the enforced limit]
         size_claimed_bytes === size_limit_bytes  with size_claimed_bytes=117, size_limit_bytes=117
```

```console
verdict  k58590bd0441e6d65  CANNOT-ASSESS  size_within_claim [README size, measured]

         cannot-assess is not a pass. A build resting on this will be refused.
```

```console
$ delphi doctor
note     3 law(s) are checked by a script, not by a proof assistant: no_runtime_dependencies, readme_matches_enforced_limit, size_within_claim. Each record says so; this is a note, not a problem.
note     1 refusal(s) on record. These are the most useful thing in the store to publish: `delphi why <name>` prints what each one was missing.
doctor: 13 node(s) sound — store chain, 0 proof file(s), 1 artifact file(s) all match their recorded hashes; 2 note(s)
```

**Notice:** `doctor` lists the three script laws as a note. That is the tool being plain about how much
weight they carry: a script law is only as good as its script.

The graph this run produced, as a page: [`cookbook/nanoid/graph.html`](cookbook/nanoid/graph.html). Its store: [`cookbook/nanoid/nodes.jsonl`](cookbook/nanoid/nodes.jsonl).

## Example 3. A repository that already publishes its audit

**The question:** the README says every proof is complete, with no `sorry` and no new axiom. Can a
stranger confirm that from the repository as published?

**What the run found:** yes, with nothing added. The repository ships a `Checks.lean` that restates its
14 headline theorems and asks Lean to print the axioms under each. `delphi law` accepted that file as it
stands, in the repository's own Lake project (leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0). A count over the sources agrees with the
README. One claim cannot be settled from this repository at all, that the results are new to Mathlib, so
it is recorded as `cannot-assess`.

This is the opposite of example 1. There the claim was true and uncheckable. Here the authors made it
checkable, and the tool's job is only to record that it was checked, by what, on which bytes.

Before the run, the project was built the way its README says (`lake build`).

### 1. Adopt it

```console
$ delphi init --name wolstenholme-zolotarev
initialised  .delphi
project      wolstenholme-zolotarev
store        .delphi/store/nodes.jsonl  (append-only, one record per line, commit it)
method       .delphi/BEST_PRACTICES.md  (generated; regenerate with `delphi best-practices`)
graph        .delphi/graph/index.html   (rewritten after every mint, private to this project)
laws         .delphi/laws/              (put your Lean files here)

Next: record the source of one number you already rely on.
  delphi evidence --kind doi --ref <doi> --quote "<the words it prints>" --where "<table or section>"

Lean files are checked in your own Lake project, found from the file, so they see your
toolchain and your libraries. With no Lean on this machine, `delphi law --lean` is refused
as unchecked, never passed. A law given with --script says on its record that a script
checked it.
```

### 2. Record what the README claims

```console
$ delphi evidence --kind file --ref README.md --quote 'There is no `sorry`, `admit` or `native_decide`, no new axiom, and no `set_option`.' --where 'lines 10 to 11, the opening section' --retrieved 2026-10-16
evidence kd2b609c91b6f259a  file:README.md
```

```console
$ delphi fact --statement 'The README says the Lean sources use no sorry, admit, native_decide, set_option or new axiom' --quantity forbidden_constructs_claimed --value 0 --unit count --condition file=README.md --condition commit=bec02d30 --evidence kd2b609c91b6f259a
fact     k56eec1882a6aaba7  forbidden_constructs_claimed = 0 count
```

```console
$ delphi evidence --kind file --ref README.md --quote 'Neither result is in Mathlib yet.' --where 'line 8, the opening paragraph' --retrieved 2026-10-16
evidence k267e48521d96f98d  file:README.md
```

```console
$ delphi fact --statement 'The README says Mathlib has no proof of either result' --quantity mathlib_proofs_claimed --value 0 --unit count --condition file=README.md --condition commit=bec02d30 --evidence k267e48521d96f98d
fact     k95315e9965f6ff5a  mathlib_proofs_claimed = 0 count
```

### 3. Ask the kernel to accept the claim as published

```console
$ delphi law --name headline_theorems_audited --informal 'Each headline theorem restated in Checks.lean is accepted by the Lean kernel on its three standard axioms, with no sorry.' --lean Checks.lean
law      kd85b43944b4bc374  headline_theorems_audited
         Checks.lean  CHECKED  axioms [Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext]  14 declaration(s) audited
         checked in this repository's own Lake project, leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0
```

**Notice:** no `delphi audit` step and no copy. The file asks for its own axioms, so there is
something to audit. The record names the Lake project the check ran in: this repository's own.

The second claim is about another repository. Its law is a statement with no check behind it yet, and
the record says exactly that:

```console
$ delphi law --name absent_upstream --informal 'A result is new to a library when a search of that library at a named commit finds no proof of it.' --script 'a search of Mathlib that nobody has recorded here'
law      kef16ad1d5d69f7c2  absent_upstream
         checked by a script, NOT by a proof assistant: a search of Mathlib that nobody has recorded here
```

### 4. Apply each law

The count, as a script anyone can read:

```js
// Do the Lean sources hold as many forbidden constructs as the README claims (none)? Counts are
// taken over code only: comments and doc-comments are removed first, because a file may talk about
// `sorry` without using it. Folders that are not the project's own source are skipped.
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';

const SKIP = new Set(['.lake', '.delphi', '.git', 'node_modules']);
const leanFiles = (dir) => fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }).flatMap((e) =>
  e.isDirectory() ? (SKIP.has(e.name) ? [] : leanFiles(path.join(dir, e.name))) : e.name.endsWith('.lean') ? [path.join(dir, e.name)] : []);

export default (values) => {
  const files = leanFiles('.');
  const count = { sorry: 0, admit: 0, native_decide: 0, set_option: 0, axiom: 0 };
  for (const f of files) {
    const code = fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8').replace(/\/-[\s\S]*?-\//g, ' ').replace(/--[^\n]*/g, ' ');
    count.sorry += (code.match(/\bsorry\b/g) ?? []).length;
    count.admit += (code.match(/\badmit\b/g) ?? []).length;
    count.native_decide += (code.match(/\bnative_decide\b/g) ?? []).length;
    count.set_option += (code.match(/\bset_option\b/g) ?? []).length;
    count.axiom += (code.match(/^\s*axiom\s+/gm) ?? []).length;
  }
  const total = Object.values(count).reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
  return {
    result: total === values.forbidden_constructs_claimed ? 'inside' : 'outside',
    detail: `${files.length} Lean file(s): ${Object.entries(count).map(([k, v]) => `${v} ${k}`).join(', ')} against ${values.forbidden_constructs_claimed} claimed`,
  };
};
```

```console
$ delphi verdict --law kd85b43944b4bc374 --fact k56eec1882a6aaba7 --requires forbidden_constructs_claimed --check .delphi/checks/no-forbidden-constructs.mjs --label 'README: no sorry, admit, native_decide, set_option or new axiom'
verdict  k867d8b30b715dee5  INSIDE  headline_theorems_audited [README: no sorry, admit, native_decide, set_option or new axiom]
         10 Lean file(s): 0 sorry, 0 admit, 0 native_decide, 0 set_option, 0 axiom against 0 claimed
```

```console
$ delphi verdict --law kef16ad1d5d69f7c2 --fact k95315e9965f6ff5a --requires mathlib_proofs_claimed --requires mathlib_proofs_found --expr 'mathlib_proofs_found === mathlib_proofs_claimed' --label 'README: not in Mathlib yet'
verdict  kf3e75e8e5c01ae1b  CANNOT-ASSESS  absent_upstream [README: not in Mathlib yet]
         missing input(s): mathlib_proofs_found
         cannot-assess is not a pass. A build resting on this will be refused.
```

### 5. Build something, or be told exactly why not

```console
$ delphi build --artifact 'a "new to Mathlib" badge' --verdict kf3e75e8e5c01ae1b
REFUSED  a "new to Mathlib" badge
         - absent_upstream (README: not in Mathlib yet): could not be assessed — missing input(s): mathlib_proofs_found

The refusal is itself a record: k6264d3abc33cb7d3. It is the shortest list of what would have to
be true for this artifact to be honest, so it is worth publishing rather than hiding.
```

```console
$ delphi build --artifact 'audit record' --verdict k867d8b30b715dee5 --file delphi-audit/REPORT.md
build    kbdc5fd6e3b25d892  audit record
         58b7bae3d0e6fdae      1078  delphi-audit/REPORT.md
```

### 6. Read it back

```console
$ delphi why badge

         - absent_upstream (README: not in Mathlib yet): could not be assessed — missing input(s): mathlib_proofs_found
  verdict  kf3e75e8e5c01ae1b  CANNOT-ASSESS  absent_upstream [README: not in Mathlib yet]  missing input(s): mathlib_proofs_found
    fact     k95315e9965f6ff5a  mathlib_proofs_claimed = 0 count  [file=README.md, commit=bec02d30]
      evidence k267e48521d96f98d  file:README.md  "Neither result is in Mathlib yet."  (line 8, the opening paragraph)
    law      kef16ad1d5d69f7c2  absent_upstream  script: a search of Mathlib that nobody has recorded here
```

## Put two commands in CI

`verify` recomputes every id and chain link. `doctor` checks what can rot without anyone touching the
store: a proof file edited after it was accepted, an artifact regenerated without a new build, a check
that has answered nothing twice.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/delphi.yml
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  record:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: 20 }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx delphi verify
      - run: npx delphi doctor
```

## What these runs do not say

- They do not say a theorem is the **right** theorem. A statement can be accepted by Lean and say
  nothing: contradictory hypotheses prove anything. That needs a reader.
- They do not say a formal statement matches the science it is named after.
- A law checked by a script is only as good as the script. Its record says a script checked it, and
  the script is printed in full above so it can be read.
- Each was run once, on one commit, on one machine. The commit is named so the run can be repeated.
- None of the three returned `outside`: every claim that could be checked held. So these runs show
  the tool refusing what cannot be checked. They do not show it catching a claim that is false; the
  fault suite covers that, with made-up inputs.
- Three repositories is three. They show the tool is not fitted to one project. They do not show it
  fits every project.

## Run them yourself

```bash
git clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout --depth 1 https://github.com/fractastical/morpholib && (cd morpholib && git sparse-checkout init --no-cone && git sparse-checkout set '/morphoeval/lean/*' && git checkout)
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ai/nanoid
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/fahad-96/wolstenholme-zolotarev && (cd wolstenholme-zolotarev && lake exe cache get && lake build)
node tracks/kernel/embed/cookbook.mjs --run all     # examples 1 and 3 need a Lean 4 toolchain
node tracks/kernel/embed/cookbook.mjs --check       # needs nothing
```
